title: What’s the best one I DIDN’T see though?? #shakespeare #theatre #broa...
transcript: ranking all 10 productions of hamlet that I've seen live first though: quick shout out to these loose adaptations or retellings which I'm not including in my ranking. and other than that, if it's not in this video, it means I didn't see it live in last place the Shakespeare in the park production from Kenny Leon a director who I generally don't vibe with it was elevated by some strong performances like Ato Blankson-Wood as Hamlet Solea Pfeiffer, the great John Douglas Thompson but overall I found it messy and unfocused. in ninth place, maybe controversially is the solo version performed by Eddie Izzard. her performance was like effortlessly brilliant and it was fun to see such an extraordinary actor play all the roles cause it's like “wow that was the best Voltemand I've ever seen” but beyond the acting showcase I don't think this play benefits from the solo show format so from a storytelling standpoint I found it to be a tough watch. in 8th place a very intimate and DIYproduction that I saw at my college and you might think it's unfair for me to include that especially because the reason it's so low on this list is because it was at a disadvantage against these professional productions but I figured I liked it more than some of the professional ones so why not? they made some really cool choices and did some great ensemble work in 7th place, the National Theatre production that I just saw at BAM starring Hiran Abeysekera a solid rendition of the play with some isolated choices that I really enjoyed but otherwise didn't leave much of an impression on me either way. next I have Sam Gold's production starring Oscar Isaac Keegan Michael Key Peter Friedman Gayle Rankin really cool to see these excellent actors in such an intimate space at the Public. the production itself was kind of a mixed bag there was a sense of experimental playfulness a kind of “anything goes” attitude that was sometimes delightful sometimes kind of exhausting and disorienting. in 5th place, a local production in Berkeley California where the roles were randomized at every performance. I do think the central gimmick pulled focus from the play more than it illuminated it but it was still a fun central gimmick and they made some other strong choices as well in *FOURTH* place, starring Ruth Negga and directed by Yael Farber it didn't necessarily reinvent the wheel but it was very dynamic and exciting and kinda captured that intense, haunting drama at the core of the story. in 3rd place a really fascinating off Broadway production starring Arian Moayed in the title role Sheri Renee Scott was also Gertrude, funny enough. it was set in Persia right before World War 1 and sections of it were strategically translated into Farsi. a little rough around the edges with some of the acting and the nitty gritty direction but this was one of the most coherent concepts I've ever seen mapped onto a Shakespeare play. to the point where I was like “maybe Hamlet is actually a play about the cultural evolution of early 20th century Persia” in 2nd place I have Thomas Ostermeier’s iconic production which is whacko and experimental and very much all about performance every character is like aware they're in a play and competing for the audience's loyalty. also maybe the most darkly comedic Hamlet I've seen where his madness kind of has him devolving into this clown-like figure desperate to entertain the audience. but in first place and frankly it's not even close we have Robert Icke’s production starring Andrew Scott undoubtedly the most tender take on this story that just incisively cuts to the devastating emotional core this is a Hamlet who just so desperately misses his father and wants to feel whole and happy again everything about this production was so grounded and crystal clear in the storytelling where every tiny detail seemed to serve the larger vision it is the best Hamlet I've ever seen or ever will see
classificationReason: Creator explicitly ranks all 10 Hamlet productions they've seen live — a classic multi-show list/ranking roundup with no single production as the primary focus.
